title: Prompt & Telemetry Lifespan Composer and Evidence Automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a composable UI + API that lets teams define lifespan (ttl) and sampling policies for prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics and produce automated, auditable evidence bundles for compliance reviewers.
objective: Allow tenants to declare per-route and per-model retention tiers (hot/nearline/archival) with deterministic sampling rules and one-click evidence export that includes hash-chained manifests and redaction flags.
background: Customers in regulated industries require fine-grained retention rules per data class (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics). Existing retention tasks are fragmented: console TTL presets, per-route attributes, and separate evidence export flows. This ticket unifies the definition surface and automation so operators can safely reduce storage while preserving forensics and auditability.
proposed_solution: Add a Retention Composer in Console to author 'lifespan blueprints' that map routes and data classes to tiers.
Expose the composer via Redwood API so infra-as-code can programmatically create blueprints.
Implement deterministic sampling algorithms (stratified by route, customer id hash, and time window) with eviction-safe anchors to ensure forensics ability when sampled.

Attach automatic evidence packaging: when a retention rule triggers deletion/eviction, capture a snapshot that includes minimal identifiers, redaction metadata, a manifest with SHA-256 hashes, and a signed audit token.
Provide a preview endpoint that simulates rule application on a retention-safe window for operator review before enforcement.
Integrate with existing region-aware residency constraints so exports respect data residency and KMS key scoping.
tradeoffs_considerations: Sampling reduces storage but may erode forensic completeness; deterministic anchors mitigate but do not eliminate this risk.
Automated evidence exports increase short-term retention for snapshots — must balance retention window and cost.
Complexity in UI may overwhelm small tenants; provide sensible presets and templates.
Preview simulation may be costly at scale; use sampled preview and cached simulation artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Console composer UI allows creation/editing of a lifespan blueprint with per-data-class rules and a named version.
API endpoints exist: POST /retention-blueprints, GET /retention-blueprints/:id/preview, POST /retention-blueprints/:id/activate.
Deterministic sampling reproducibility test suite with 3s latency for sample decision under load.
Automated evidence package generation that includes manifest.json, per-item redaction metadata, and a signed audit token stored in tenant-scoped S3.
Region-aware export honors residency; any export attempt across regions fails with auditable error.
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating purge with evidence package and successful import into forensic toolchain.
Docs and runbook for compliance reviewers and SOC on how to verify exported evidence.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal tenant + 2 enterprise customers opt-in. Instrument metrics and collect feedback (2 weeks).
Beta: expose to public console with opt-in default false; provide migration tool for existing TTL rules (4 weeks).
GA: enable presets for common regulated frameworks and provide on-demand evidence export SLA (after beta + 3 weeks).
metrics_and_signals: % of routes with explicit retention blueprints
monthly storage delta attributable to sampling/eviction
